transcript.text: Indesit washer dryer washes fine but the drying cycle doesn't get warm at all, clothes come out cold and wet after 2 hours. Model is XWDE 96 something.

Please switch the machine off and unplug it first for safety. Drying sends fluff and condensed water out through the pump, so a clogged pump filter at the bottom front can stop drying and cause leaks. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water may come out. Unscrew the filter slowly so the water comes out gradually. You might find helpful details in the picture shown below. Was the filter full of fluff or debris (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the pump filter is" — The pump filter is usually behind a flap at the bottom front. Turn the machine off and drain any water first, then twist the filter out to clear it. Typical location — your machine may differ.]
I haven't checked the filter yet. Is that likely to cause no heat though? The fan runs and the drum tumbles fine, it's just stone cold. No burning smell and nothing's tripped, by the way.

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven't had a chance yet. Drying sends fluff and condensed water out through the pump, so a clogged pump filter at the bottom front stops drying and can make water back up and leak. Switch the machine off and unplug it first. Put towels down and have a shallow tray or baking dish ready, as several litres of water can come out. Unscrew the filter slowly so the water comes out gradually. Was the filter full of fluff or debris (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
I haven't done the filter yet, so I can't say what's in it. I'm still not sure how a blocked filter would stop the heating when the fan and drum work fine. Is there anything else it could be?

Thanks for letting us know about the drain filter status. To help narrow down why there is no heat, please check that a proper drying programme has been selected after the wash cycle finishes, rather than just a short timed dry or a setting with low dryness. Was drying not selected or set too short (and have you changed it), or was a full drying programme set?
It was on standard cotton dry, timed 120 min, so not a cool or air dry setting. Load was about 4kg.

[Heading: Drying heater or its thermostat]
Thanks for letting me know about the issue during the full drying cycle. With the washing side working fine but no heat at all on a drying programme, the drying heater or its thermostat is likely the cause. This is a separate component from the wash heater. I am not recommending you replace any parts yourself. The next step needs internal electrical testing, so this is the point to bring in a qualified appliance engineer.
